document.title: Ambassador Dean's Cable- "Subject: Meeting with Prime Minister Gandhi, December 6"
document.authors: Ambassador John Gunther Dean, U.S. Embassy New Delhi
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), A New Phase in the Great Game: U.S., Soviets, India, Pakistan vied to shape a new Afghanistan in late 1980s | National Security Archive
document.note: Private conversation focused on Gandhi's summit with Gorbachev and concerns about arming the mujahedin. Gandhi praises Gorbachev, criticizes Weinberger's visit and AWACS for Pakistan, and mentions co-mingling of Iran arms sale funds with mujahedin funding.

mentions.quote: I MET BY CHANCE PRIME MINISTER GANDHI. HE ASKED ME TO JOIN HIM IN A CORNER
I REPLIED THAT IT WOULD BE HELPFUL IF I COULD GET A READ-OUT ON HIS DISCUSSION WITH GORBACHEV
THE PRIME MINISTER REPLIED THAT THE SUBJECT HAD COME UP IN THE PRIVATE TALKS WITH GORBACHEV
GANDHI HAD MET THROUGH HIS MOTHER PREVIOUS SOVIET LEADERS

persons.name: Mikhail Gorbachev
persons.role: Soviet leader (General Secretary), visited Delhi November 1986
organizations: Communist Party of the Soviet Union

mentions.quote: GORBACHEV WAS "A MUCH MORE PRAGMATIC LEADER- WILLING TO EXPLORE NEW APPROACHES TO OLD PROBLEMS."
PRESIDENT REAGAN'S LETTER OF NOVEMBER 21 REGARDING AFGHANISTAN
WOULD EITHER PASS ON THE GIST OF THIS DISCUSSION THROUGH FOREIGN SECRETARY VENKATESWARAN

persons.role: U.S. Secretary of Defense; visited India ca. Sept/Oct 1986

mentions.quote: ISSUES WHICH HAD BEEN RAISED WITH THE SECRETARY OF DEFENSE DURING HIS VISIT MORE THAN TWO MONTHS AGO

events.description: Ambassador Dean met PM Gandhi by chance at a wedding reception for about 15 minutes; discussed Afghanistan, Gorbachev, tech transfer, AWACS, Iran arms.
President Reagan sent a letter to Gandhi regarding Afghanistan.
Gorbachev-Gandhi talks in Delhi about two weeks earlier, including private conversations touching on Afghanistan.
PM's office said Gandhi would be out of Delhi Dec 17-20, complicating a meeting with Solarz.
Ambassador Dean met PM Gandhi by chance at a wedding reception for a 15-minute talk covering Afghanistan, Weinberger visit, AWACS, arms to Iran, Solarz visit.
President Reagan sent a letter to Gandhi regarding Afghanistan.
Gandhi and Gorbachev held talks in Delhi, including many hours of private conversation, reportedly discussing Afghanistan.
Defense Secretary Weinberger visited India and discussed technology transfer issues; no US reply received after eight weeks.
English-language Indian press ran front-page articles saying the Pentagon opposes know-how transfer to India.
PM's office said Gandhi would be out of Delhi Dec 17-20, jeopardizing a meeting with Solarz.

sources_cited: International press reports on AWACS for Pakistan
key_claims: Gandhi viewed Gorbachev as a more pragmatic and tactically different Soviet leader though pursuing the same goals.
Gandhi said Afghanistan was raised in his private talks with Gorbachev, but gave no details.
Gandhi complained of U.S. silence on technology transfer issues raised during Weinberger's visit.
Indian advisors read the AWACS-for-Pakistan announcement as a sign of U.S. disinterest in better ties with India.
Gandhi noted apparent co-mingling of Iran arms-sale profits with U.S. and Saudi funds for the mujahedin.
Gandhi said the Saudis were apparently to fund AWACS for Pakistan.
Dean linked the Soviet occupation of Afghanistan to the U.S.-Pakistan relationship.
